overview: Centrica is a UK- and Ireland-focused integrated energy company operating across three segments: Retail (British Gas and Bord Gais energy supply and home/business services to over 10 million customers), Optimisation (Centrica Energy gas, power and LNG trading plus renewable energy trading and optimisation), and Infrastructure (nuclear generation including a 20% UK nuclear fleet stake and a 15% equity stake in Sizewell C, gas storage/production via Spirit Energy and Rough, the Grain LNG terminal, flexible/peaking power generation, and the in-house Meter Asset Provider). The strategy, explicitly branded 'Transforming Centrica,' is to pivot the portfolio away from volatile commodity trading and gas production toward regulated, contracted and rateable infrastructure earnings (Sizewell B/C, MAP, Grain LNG, Severn CCGT) that deliver more stable, predictable cash flow.

business_model.summary: Revenue is generated from (1) retail energy supply and home/business services billed to ~10m UK and Irish customers (recurring, regulated-margin, price-cap-constrained), (2) wholesale gas/power/LNG trading and optimisation (transactional, margin/spread-driven, highly volatile year to year), and (3) infrastructure assets earning contracted or regulated returns (nuclear generation, gas storage/production, LNG terminal capacity, smart meter rental income). Management now presents results on an adjusted EBITDA/adjusted operating profit basis because statutory operating profit swings heavily from one-off exceptional items and mark-to-market re-measurement of derivative energy contracts (e.g. FY2023 statutory operating margin ~24.6% vs FY2025 ~0.5%, and 2025 vs 2024 moved from a GBP1,703m to GBP106m statutory operating profit on a GBP708m net exceptional/re-measurement swing) -- the adjusted figures (GBP814m adjusted operating profit, GBP1,417m adjusted EBITDA for FY2025) are the more reliable lens on underlying trading.

revenue_streams.name: Retail (Home Energy Supply, Home Services, Business)
Infrastructure (Nuclear, Spirit Energy gas, Grain LNG, Power, MAP)
revenue_streams.trend: mixed - legacy gas production declining, new rateable infrastructure (MAP, Sizewell, Grain LNG, Severn) growing

business_model.customer_type: B2C mass-market retail (10m+ households) and B2B/SME business energy and services customers, plus wholesale counterparties (power/gas/LNG trading) and government/regulatory counterparties for infrastructure (RAB, CfD, capacity market contracts)
business_model.geographic_mix: Primarily UK, with Republic of Ireland (Bord Gais) retail and power generation (Whitegate, Athlone/Dublin peakers), gas/power/LNG trading across 29 power markets and 19 gas hubs in Europe and the US, and a new North American (New York) trading office

competitive_position.market_position: British Gas was overtaken by Octopus Energy as the UK's single largest energy supplier by 2025 (Octopus ~23.7% vs British Gas ~23.6% of the retail market, with British Gas's lead historically resting on gas-only dominance); Centrica remains the largest and most diversified integrated UK energy group given its nuclear, LNG, gas storage and trading businesses alongside retail, and is a FTSE 100 constituent (~GBP9bn market cap).

moat_factors.description: British Gas's 200-year heritage and 10m+ customer base, 7,000+ field engineers, and improving NPS/Trustpilot scores (4.4 stars) support retention, though brand has eroded against digital-native challengers

20% stake in UK's existing nuclear fleet, 15% RAB-backed equity stake in Sizewell C (10.8% real allowed return), Sizewell B CfD (GBP70.50/MWh from 2035), and >50% of UK gas storage capacity (Rough) are scarce, long-life, regulator-sanctioned assets that are very difficult for a new entrant to replicate

Scale in gas/power/LNG trading (271 LNG cargoes in 2025, 19.5GW renewable/flexible capacity under management) gives optimisation capability smaller suppliers lack, but this also increases earnings volatility

New Ofgem capital adequacy rules for suppliers (introduced after the 2021-22 wave of supplier failures) raise barriers to entry/survival in retail, benefiting well-capitalised incumbents like Centrica, though implementation has been slow and inconsistent per management

weaknesses: Lost title of UK's largest single energy supplier to Octopus Energy; underlying UK energy customer numbers have been roughly flat to slightly declining
Retail adjusted operating margin is thin (2.6-3.3%) and highly exposed to bad debt, weather and the Ofgem price cap's commodity-cost allowance mechanics
Optimisation/trading earnings are volatile and have materially underperformed in 2025-26 (Centrica Energy EBITDA roughly halved in FY2025, with 2027 guidance also lowered)
Legacy North Sea gas production (Spirit Energy) is in managed decline/divestment, removing a previously significant profit contributor
No long-term monopoly or network-effect moat in retail supply, which remains a commoditized, switchable product

growth_drivers: Pivot to regulated/contracted 'rateable' infrastructure earnings: Sizewell C (GBP1.3bn capped equity investment, 12%+ IRR), Sizewell B 20-year life extension via CfD, Heysham 1/Hartlepool life extensions, Isle of Grain LNG terminal (50% stake, highly contracted to 2045)
Meter Asset Provider (MAP) smart meter rollout - 2.3m+ meters under management, run-rate EBITDA ~GBP60m/year and growing, 'unrivalled installation pipeline'

New flexible/dispatchable power generation to meet rising UK electricity demand - Severn CCGT acquisition (850MW, GBP367m), Irish gas peakers (Athlone, Dublin, planned Galway OCGT), positioned near growing data centre demand in South Wales
Electrification and data centre-driven UK power demand growth, which management explicitly cites as a structural tailwind for baseload, flexible generation and behind-the-meter solutions
Advanced/modular nuclear optionality via X-energy partnership (up to 6GW of high-temperature gas reactors, Xe-100 submitted to UK Generic Design Assessment)
Morecambe Net Zero carbon storage project (potential for UK's largest carbon storage hub) and hydrogen opportunities in the Humber region

Technology-led transformation programme targeting ~GBP0.5bn underlying cost reduction (flat nominal opex ex bad debt/depreciation through the decade) and ~1,300 role reductions, funded by ~GBP0.6bn of investment
Long-term financial targets: GBP1.7bn Group adjusted EBITDA by 2028, rising to GBP2.0bn by 2030, with adjusted EPS targeted to double by 2030 versus 2025

business.risk: Loss of retail market leadership and intensifying competition
business.description: Octopus Energy has overtaken British Gas as the UK's largest supplier; digital-native and vertically-integrated challengers continue to pressure retail margins and customer retention

Centrica's retail bad debt charge rose to GBP418m in FY2025 (from GBP369m) and UK residential bad debt was >4% of revenue in H1 2026; industry-wide consumer energy debt is projected to reach ~GBP7bn in 2026, a structural risk management says needs a coordinated Ofgem/government response

business.risk: Centrica Energy (trading/optimisation) earnings volatility and underperformance
business.description: Optimisation EBITDA nearly halved in FY2025 (GBP196m vs GBP381m) on weak gas/power trading and EU storage-target distortions; 2027 guidance for the segment was lowered to ~2025/2026 levels (around GBP250m), well below the GBP300-400m medium-term target
Spirit Energy production fell 21% in FY2025 as the Group exits North Sea production via disposals (Cygnus to Ithaca, remaining Spirit assets sold to Serica Energy), with completion expected H2 2026
Hartlepool reactor outages cut FY2025 nuclear generation by 12%; unplanned outages at ageing nuclear and gas assets are a recurring earnings drag

financial.risk: Free cash flow swung negative amid step-up in investment
financial.description: Group free cash flow was a GBP167m outflow in FY2025 (from GBP989m inflow in FY2024) and a further GBP570m outflow in H1 2026, as capital expenditure accelerated to fund Sizewell C, Grain LNG, Severn CCGT and MAP; adjusted net cash fell from GBP2,858m (FY2024) to GBP1,487m (FY2025) to GBP709m (H1 2026)
IAS 19 net pension deficit widened to GBP295m at end-2025 (from GBP21m) on actuarial losses; annual deficit contributions of ~GBP150m (2026) and ~GBP140m (2027) are required
FY2025 statutory results included GBP508m of impairments, largely on late-life gas fields and nuclear investment (ex-Sizewell C), driven by lower forecast power/gas prices

regulatory.risk: Ofgem price cap and retail regulation
regulatory.description: Retail margins are structurally capped by Ofgem's price cap mechanism; commodity-cost under/over-recovery timing (e.g. backwardated curve causing an expected H2 2026 under-recovery) creates working-capital and earnings timing risk

The Electricity Generator Levy (45% on nuclear/renewables wholesale revenue above an inflation-adjusted GBP75/MWh threshold) cost Centrica GBP19m in FY2025 and GBP511m cumulatively since 2023; the broader Energy Profits Levy on oil & gas was raised by the Labour government in 2025, and Centrica/peers have faced political pressure over sector profitability

British Gas settled with Ofgem in May 2026 (GBP20m into the Voluntary Redress Fund, customer redress for 2018-21, up to GBP70m of debt write-offs for vulnerable customers); reputational and policy risk around vulnerable-customer treatment persists

regulatory.risk: Supplier capital adequacy and sector instability
regulatory.description: Management flagged continuing supplier failures (Rebel Energy, Tomato Energy) and inconsistent Ofgem enforcement of capital adequacy rules as a systemic risk that could again require Centrica to absorb Supplier-of-Last-Resort customers

regulatory.risk: Gas storage/security of supply policy uncertainty
regulatory.description: Rough storage operations were paused in 2025 on uneconomic spreads pending a UK government consultation on gas storage policy; EU mandatory storage-filling targets and their post-2027 evolution also affect European gas economics

macro.description: Gas, power and LNG price levels and spreads materially affect Optimisation and Infrastructure earnings; geopolitical shocks (e.g. Middle East conflict disrupting LNG shipping/insurance in H1 2026) directly hit trading performance
Unseasonably warm weather reduced FY2025 Home Energy Supply profitability by an estimated GBP80m and continued to affect H1 2026 results

macro.risk: UK interest rates and cash balances
macro.description: Lower UK interest rates and shrinking cash balances (post-buyback, post-capex ramp) reduced net finance income, a modest EPS headwind
Management explicitly flags political debate over net zero policy and targets as a factor affecting trading dynamics and investment certainty

macro_factors.industry_outlook: UK energy system transitioning toward electrification, renewables and nuclear baseload, with structurally rising demand for flexible/dispatchable generation and data-centre-driven electricity growth; retail supply remains a thin-margin, regulated, highly competitive market with industry-wide bad debt at record levels
macro_factors.cyclicality: Mixed - Retail is relatively defensive (essential service, price-cap-smoothed) but sensitive to weather and bad debt cycles; Optimisation/trading is highly cyclical and volatile with commodity markets; Infrastructure is shifting toward long-duration, contracted/regulated cash flows (lower cyclicality going forward)
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - net finance income/cost is sensitive to UK rates and the size of Centrica's cash balance, which has shrunk materially as buybacks paused and capex increased

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 interim results: adjusted EBITDA fell 18% YoY to GBP737m, adjusted EPS 6.8p (H1 2025: 7.0p); shares fell ~2-3% as market focused on lowered 2027 Centrica Energy outlook and elevated bad debt; interim dividend raised 9% to 2.0p

Sizewell B life extension to 2055 confirmed, underpinned by a 20-year CfD with a GBP70.50/MWh strike price (2025 prices, CPI-indexed) from April 2035; Heysham 1 and Hartlepool nuclear stations' lives extended to March 2030

British Gas settled with Ofgem over legacy prepayment meter installation practices: GBP20m into the Voluntary Redress Fund, customer redress for 2018-21, and up to GBP70m of vulnerable-customer debt write-offs; management said no impact to 2026 guidance

Completed acquisition of the 850MW Severn CCGT power station (South Wales) for GBP367m net consideration, adding dispatchable capacity near growing data-centre power demand; expected EBITDA of GBP30-60m/year from 2027

Submitted application to the UK's Advanced Nuclear Framework (ANF) process for the X-energy advanced modular reactor partnership; X-energy separately submitted its Xe-100 reactor design to the UK Generic Design Assessment process in June 2026

FY2025 results: statutory operating profit collapsed to GBP106m (from GBP1,703m in 2024) on exceptional items/re-measurements; adjusted operating profit GBP814m (down from GBP1,552m); GBP508m of impairments on gas fields and nuclear (ex-Sizewell C); full-year dividend raised to 5.5p; GBP2bn cumulative share buyback programme completed, now paused in favour of investment

Completed acquisition of the Isle of Grain LNG terminal from National Grid (50% stake, ~GBP200m equity investment, ~GBP1.5bn enterprise value), highly contracted to 2045; agreed sale of Centrica Business Solutions Italia/BV to Joulz B.V.; agreed sale of remaining Spirit Energy North Sea assets to Serica Energy (completion expected H2 2026)
Completed sale of a 46.25% interest in the Cygnus gas field to Ithaca Energy for GBP123m, part of the broader Spirit Energy exit from North Sea production
Octopus Energy overtook British Gas to become the UK's single largest energy supplier (c.23.7% vs c.23.6% of the retail market), ending British Gas's historical overall-market lead

Signed GBP20bn, 10-year gas supply partnership with Equinor (5bcm/year to 2035) to bolster UK gas security of supply; signed Joint Development Agreement with X-energy for advanced modular nuclear reactors

items.target: towards the lower end of GBP500m-GBP800m
items.notes: Guided to the lower end of the prior range amid elevated bad debt and a backwardated commodity curve implying under-recovery of costs in H2 2026

Management reaffirmed confidence in delivering ~GBP250m for FY2026 despite a weak H1, but flagged Centrica Energy EBITDA in 2027 is now expected to be around 2025/2026 levels rather than stepping up toward the GBP300-400m medium-term range
Includes MAP, Sizewell C and Grain LNG ('rateable' infrastructure) contributing around GBP175m of this
Reflects lower cash balances following buybacks and capex ramp-up
Consistent with the ~GBP4bn investment programme through 2028 (Sizewell C, Grain LNG, MAP, Severn CCGT, Irish peakers)
Long-term target underpinned by nuclear life extensions and rateable infrastructure ramp-up; cost base held flat in nominal terms for five years

items.target: ~GBP0.6bn (GBP0.4bn opex + GBP0.2bn capex) to deliver ~GBP0.5bn underlying cost reduction
items.notes: Includes ~1,300 role reductions; costs expensed through business performance, not treated as exceptional

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Chris O'Shea: 'Volatility across energy markets has created challenges in some parts of our business, and some of our delivery has been slower than we would like... Long-term targets unchanged - GBP2.0bn adjusted EBITDA and doubling EPS by 2030.' Management reaffirmed the long-term 2028/2030 targets and FY2026 guidance ranges while explicitly lowering the implied 2027 trajectory for Centrica Energy (Optimisation) to around current levels rather than the GBP300-400m medium-term range, citing a wide range of possible outcomes and continued market volatility.

bull_case: Clear, well-funded strategic pivot from volatile commodity trading/production toward long-duration, contracted/regulated infrastructure earnings (Sizewell B & C, Grain LNG, MAP, Severn CCGT) should structurally lower earnings volatility and support the re-rating implied by management's 2028/2030 EBITDA and EPS-doubling targets

Structural UK demand tailwinds -- electrification, data centre growth, and the need for new dispatchable and nuclear baseload capacity -- play directly to Centrica's existing nuclear stakes, new gas peakers, and the Severn CCGT acquisition sited near data-centre demand in South Wales

Scarce, hard-to-replicate regulated assets (20% of UK's nuclear fleet, 15% RAB-backed Sizewell C stake with 10.8% real allowed return, >50% of UK gas storage capacity) provide downside protection and visible long-term cash flows once construction/ramp phases complete

Strong balance sheet discipline track record: GBP2bn cumulative share buybacks completed by early 2026 (about a quarter of shares outstanding), rising dividend (5.5p FY2025, 9% increase in H1 2026 interim to 2.0p), and ~GBP5bn of committed liquidity provide resilience and optionality to resume returns once the investment phase matures

Retail operational improvements (record customer satisfaction/NPS, Trustpilot 'Excellent' 4.4 stars, falling complaints, growing membership scheme) and a GBP0.5bn cost-reduction transformation programme support margin recovery independent of commodity cycles
bear_case: Centrica Energy (Optimisation/trading) earnings have deteriorated sharply and 2027 guidance was cut below the medium-term GBP300-400m EBITDA target, raising doubt about the path to the 2028/2030 Group EBITDA targets and about the durability of trading-desk profitability generally

British Gas has lost its position as the UK's single largest energy supplier to Octopus Energy, and industry-wide bad debt (rising to ~GBP7bn sector-wide) continues to erode thin retail margins, with Centrica's own retail bad debt charge climbing each period

Free cash flow has swung sharply negative (GBP167m outflow FY2025, GBP570m outflow H1 2026) as capital investment accelerates, depleting net cash from GBP2,858m (FY2024) to GBP709m (H1 2026) and pausing the buyback program just as commodity and trading headwinds persist

Heavy and growing regulatory/political tax burden -- Electricity Generator Levy on nuclear/renewables, a raised Energy Profits Levy on oil & gas peers, Ofgem price cap constraints, and the prepayment-meter redress settlement -- signals continued windfall-tax and conduct-regulation risk for a UK energy incumbent

Execution risk is high and multi-year: Sizewell C construction, Sizewell B CfD ramp from 2035, advanced nuclear (X-energy) regulatory approval through 2029, and Irish peaker commissioning delays all push most new-infrastructure earnings out several years, leaving the stock reliant on management's long-dated targets being delivered without further slippage or impairment
